parsed.explanation: The combined regime is split: this state/province sits in the documented 'Most Protective' tier, with a current care shield law, gender-identity public-accommodation and hate-crime protections, self-attestation marker changes, an X option, no local bathroom ban, and repealed criminalisation. But every visitor first passes the national layer, which the dossier documents as actively hostile: the foreign ministry redefined sex as birth sex, stopped X markers, instructs officers to refuse applications where sex is doubted and to consider lifetime fraud findings, and a Feb 2025 cable tags trans-related cases; multiple allied governments issued travel advisories after detentions. National custody practices — forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse of trans immigration detainees, conversion-model prison policies — are documented and current. Entry screening and custody are universal-exposure exposures with no effective remedy shown; the state layer protects daily life and care, and cannot displace the border or federal custody. This places it below protective anchors and near the mid-elevated anchors where documented universal exposure coexists with otherwise functioning institutions.

entry_documents.exposure: National passport rules void X markers and require birth-sex entries; visa cable directs refusal where sex is doubted and flags possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; trans travellers reported with confiscated/blocked passports and stranded; allied governments' advisories follow detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic; limited waivers exist; passport policy remains under litigation and prior 1992 policy stood for decades.
entry_documents.interaction: Federal entry screening reaches every arrival in this state/province; state protections cannot operate at the border.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau adopted conversion-model policies for trans inmates (hair, hormone removal); bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner counts; immigration custody shows forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented for visitors in custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor arrested locally (e.g. misdemeanour) could pass into federal or mixed custody governed by national rules; state hate-crime and panic-defence law do not govern placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars trans access to federally funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; 20+ state/provinces have bathroom bans, several criminal; arrests documented (capitol trespass arrest, 24h men's ward).
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province is not listed on the bathroom-restriction inventory; local public accommodations protected since 2006; X markers available locally.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal buildings and federal facility rules still apply inside the state/province; state protection covers state and private settings not otherwise banned.

care_services.exposure: National orders framing youth care as 'mutilation', funding freezes, proposed insurance bars, hospital record subpoenas of patients under 19; disabled or enjoined in part but trajectory documented.
care_services.protection: Current state shield law (Sept 2026) protects visitors obtaining lawful care; mandatory insurance coverage and 2016 nondiscrimination rule documented; conversion-therapy ban since 2018.
care_services.interaction: A visiting adult or accompanying minor from a ban state/province can lawfully obtain care here, shielded from home-state and some national charges; invocation mechanics undocumented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National documents frame 'radical gender ideology' and 'radically pro-transgender' groups as security targets; counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'neutralization' of pro-trans ideological groups; agencies remove trans references and criminalise facilitating minors' transitions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Documents state powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders enjoined; state/province enforces protective statutes since 2005.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State police operate under state equality law, but federal investigative authority over speech, schools and advocacy reaches everywhere, chilling travel with a trans minor.

minors_guardians.exposure: Executive order directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating a minor's social transition; youth-care banned in 27 state/provinces; proposed national insurance bar for under-18 care; schools investigated.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield law protects visitors' care; state anti-bullying and education-equity laws cover gender identity; conversion therapy banned for minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a guardian faces state-protected care locally but federal exposure if return transit, national records, or enforcement at other levels intervenes.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state/province-specific violence figures; national hate-crime data covers sexual orientation, not trans specifically; state enforcement intensity not documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime statute covers gender identity/expression; panic defences abolished; anti-discrimination law operative since 2005; local police not documented as targeting trans people.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State recourse exists on paper and by long enactment, but actual prosecution practice is undocumented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Whether shield-law invocation works for visitors is undocumented; national passport policy in live litigation creates moving exposure; state X-marker practice alongside national restrictions unclear; no state violence or prosecution data.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ on documents; civil-liberties litigation ongoing; state commission on equal treatment.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions at the border (document outcomes) cannot be offset by state remedies the traveller reaches only after entry.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier of unremedied universal exposure, but this jurisdiction's exposure concentrates at the federal border/custody layer while its local layer actively protects (shield law, accommodations law), unlike 0.35-A where public-building exclusion applies locally and courts confirm exclusions. That places this jurisdiction somewhat above 0.35-A.

0.55-B has local hostility with partial remedies under an accepting parent. Here the parent regime is the hostile layer (border fraud refusals, custody abuse) while the local layer is the protective one; the worst documented feature is state-imposed universal entry screening plus documented custody abuse, heavier than 0.55-B's ferry refusals, so this sits below it.

0.75-C has a dead-letter statute, accepted documents and no universal rule. Here universal national entry-document scrutiny and documented custody harm are live, not latent, so this cannot reach 0.75 despite the state/province's extensive protections.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime a traveller encounters is two-tiered. After entry, the state/province offers documented, functioning protections: a current care shield relevant to visitors and travelling families, accommodation and hate-crime coverage, easy marker changes, and no facility ban — daily-life exposure is low. But the journey begins at the national border, where the dossier documents a birth-sex document regime, X-marker elimination, officer instructions to refuse doubtful cases and consider lifetime fraud findings, stranded travellers, foreign advisories and detentions — a universal exposure every trans visitor carries, with litigation unresolved and no shown remedy. If a visitor enters custody at any level, documented national practices (conversion-model prison policy, immigration-custody forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse) are severe and current. Federal threat-framing of pro-trans advocacy adds exposure for out travellers and guardians of trans minors. State protections mitigate the visit but cannot displace federal entry screening or custody; the combination lands in elevated risk, near the 0.45–0.55 anchors.
